Thomas Malory, Le Morte d’Arthur.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/thomas-malory/le-morte-darthur

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Thomas Malory (author), died 1471.
- A. W. Pollard (annotator, role code wfw), died 1944.
- William Caxton (writer of preface), died 1492.

First publication of the text used (SE colophon: 'Le Morte d’Arthur was published in 1485 by Thomas Malory.').

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published before 1931 (SE colophon: 'Le Morte d’Arthur was published in 1485 by Thomas Malory.'), so it is in the United States public domain. The edition's rights statement below says the same.
- Country of origin: the facts do not fix the country of first publication. The possible countries are the United Kingdom, Ireland, the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, India and South Africa. Each of them has a term of life + 70 years or less. The last person to die died in 1944, so the text entered the public domain in each of them on 1 January 2015.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
